significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(ii) causal conclusion that "benign downstream fine-tuning erodes safety because it perturbs the refusal direction's supporting parameters" and that preserving this computation prevents harmful compliance with little task loss; this establishes both a fine-tuning phenomenon and a mechanism, but remains bounded mainly to refusal behavior rather than stating a scaling law or decomposition of multiple safety failures. It would connect the safety degradation documented by Qi et al. (2023), Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, to the refusal mechanism characterized by Arditi et al. (2024), Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction, thereby fixing a concrete explanation and fine-tuning decision rather than merely another correlation. The branches are distinguishable: failure despite preserved projections would rule out the identified refusal subspace as a sufficient anchor and favor distributed or changing safety mechanisms, although phrases such as "far better" and "minimal task-performance cost" leave the effect threshold somewhat underspecified. After topic substitution, generic mechanistic LLM safety would not merit this score; the specific preservation-to-safety causal claim adds value, but its single-behavior form keeps it near the topic median.

reach.justification: The transferable handle is the proposed "regularizer during downstream fine-tuning that penalizes changes to the model's refusal-direction computation," specifically preserving "projection behavior on a small safety anchor set." It is ex ante because it operates while a model is customized, before post-fine-tuning harmful compliance occurs, and could therefore be used by model developers or deployers rather than only by interpretability researchers. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion would provide a design rule—preserve refusal-subspace projections to retain refusal safety—but not predicted numerical effects across architectures; its asserted scope covers several benign fine-tuning classes while expressly conceding that adversarial fine-tuning and "non-refusal safety behaviors" may fall outside it. Topic substitution would remove the actionable training-time anchor and would not sustain this score; the named preventive handle and practitioner action window justify reach above the topic's default post-hoc probe.
